h1:
Suphan Buri from Bangkok
A Full-Day In-Town Day Trip
intro: Suphan Buri sits just about 100 km from Bangkok — an hour and a half to two hours by car — which makes it an easy day trip you can do without staying overnight. This plan focuses on the town centre: short drives, several stops close together, and you're back in Bangkok before evening.

blocks.html: A lot of people skip Suphan Buri, assuming it's too far or there's nothing to see — but it's actually a really well-rounded day-trip destination. The main sights sit close together, never more than 15–20 minutes apart by car, and you get old temples, an observation tower, a Chinese dragon park, and a century-old market all in one trip. It's ideal if you want to get out of Bangkok and change the scenery for a day without any complicated planning.

blocks.text: How to Get There from Bangkok

blocks.html: It's roughly 100 km from Bangkok to central Suphan Buri, about 1.5 to 2 hours if you drive yourself. The main route is Highway 340 (Bang Bua Thong–Suphan Buri), a straightforward run that's well suited to anyone who wants to hit several stops in a single day.

items: Drive yourself — by far the easiest option for a day trip, since the in-town sights are spread out and you can move between them at your own pace. Parking is available at almost every stop.
Minivan — board at Mo Chit 2 bus terminal or the new Southern (Sai Tai Mai) terminal. Fares run around 100 THB each way and the trip takes about 1 hour 40 minutes.

Coach (Suphan Tour) — departs Mo Chit 2 from early morning, around 06:30, through to evening. Tickets start at roughly 140–180 THB. Works well if you're only visiting the town centre and happy to walk or grab a motorbike taxi between spots.

blocks.title: A note on timing
blocks.html: If you leave Bangkok before 8 am, you'll reach Suphan Buri around 9–10 am, giving you a full day of sightseeing and a head start on the evening traffic. For the drive home, aim to leave Suphan Buri before 5 pm to make it easier.

blocks.html: This plan keeps in-town driving to a minimum: start with temples in the morning, climb the tower for a view over the town, walk through the dragon park, then finish at Sam Chuk Market in the afternoon before heading back to Bangkok. Trim stops to match your energy and interests.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Morning: temples + a view over town

items.activity: Arrive in Suphan Buri, start at Wat Pa Lelai Worawihan
items.note: The town's landmark temple, home to a large seated Luang Pho To Buddha image inside a tall hall. Entry is around 30 THB for Thais and 150 THB for foreigners. Parking is easy; allow about 45 minutes.

items.activity: Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat — the old prang
items.note: Close to Wat Pa Lelai, just a few minutes' drive away. It has an ancient main prang and Buddha images to pay respects to.
A tall observation tower with 360-degree views over Suphan Buri. Adult entry is around 30 THB. It sits inside Chaloem Phatra Rachini Park and is open roughly 10:00–18:00.

items.activity: Lunch — boat noodles or local dishes
items.note: Suphan Buri is known for its boat noodles. You'll find plenty of shops around town, with bowls running about 15–25 THB each, so ordering several won't hurt your wallet.
A reconstructed Chinese village with a museum inside a giant dragon, and lots of photo spots. Plan on about 1–1.5 hours to walk around. Check the entry times for the dragon museum before you go.

items.activity: Drive to Sam Chuk Market (the century-old market)
items.note: About 20–25 km from the town centre, roughly 30 minutes' drive. It's an old wooden market along the Tha Chin River — walk through for local snacks and souvenirs.

items.activity: Pick up souvenirs at Sam Chuk — sponge cake, dried snacks
items.note: Soft Chinese sponge cake (salee) and old-fashioned sweets are easy to find in the market — popular souvenirs to bring back to Bangkok.
Leaving before 5 pm helps you avoid the traffic heading into the city. You'll reach Bangkok around 7–8 pm.

items.name: Wat Pa Lelai Worawihan
items.blurb: The town's historic landmark temple, with a large seated Luang Pho To Buddha in a tall hall. Locals come to pay respects regularly, and it's easy to reach in the centre of town.

items.name: Banharn–Jaemsai Tower
items.blurb: A tall observation tower in a public park with 360-degree views over the town. Good for photos and a mid-morning rest, and the entry fee is cheap.

items.name: Dragon Descendants Park
items.blurb: A reconstructed Chinese village with a museum inside a giant dragon. Lots of photo angles and a hit with kids — an easy place to wander.

items.name: Sam Chuk Market
items.blurb: A century-old wooden market on the Tha Chin River — walk through for local food, old-style sweets, and souvenirs, all with a retro feel.

blocks.html: Suphan Buri is a town where you can eat local for very little. The standouts are boat noodles, yam-style noodles, and the old-fashioned sweets at Sam Chuk Market. We've picked the shops and dishes that locals and visitors talk about most.

items.name: Suphan Buri Boat Noodles
items.blurb: The province's signature dish — a rich, dark broth in small bowls you can order several of. Easy to find in town, and a filling, cheap lunch.

items.name: Jek Ao Wonton Noodles (Sam Chuk)
items.blurb: A legendary wonton-noodle shop in Sam Chuk Market, open for more than 80 years and now run by the third generation on the same Teochew recipe. Soft noodles in a well-balanced broth.

items.name: Rang Sriroj — Lotus-Leaf Rice & Dry Yam Noodles
items.blurb: The only place in Sam Chuk serving lotus-leaf-wrapped rice and dry yam noodles. Open over 40 years, these signature plates are a must-order when you're at the market.

items.name: Mae Kim Liang Sponge Cake
items.blurb: Freshly made sponge cake (salee) — soft, fluffy, and fragrant. A best-selling souvenir in Sam Chuk that travels back to Bangkok well, and it's inexpensive.

items.name: Yam Noodles with Soft-Boiled Egg
items.blurb: Old-style tom yam noodles in a thick, concentrated broth, served with a soft-boiled egg. The bold flavour pairs well with the noodles, and you'll find it in Sam Chuk Market.

items.name: Old-Fashioned Sweets at Sam Chuk Market
items.blurb: Fresh egg-and-butter cake, rolled wafers (thong muan), kalamae toffee, miang kham, and golden Thai sweets — graze your way down the market. Great for picking up a few to take home.

blocks.title: If you have more than one day
blocks.html: Want to add some nature? You can stop at Bueng Chawak Chaloemphrakiat (outside town, about 40–50 km away), which has an aquarium and a large walk-in aviary. But trying to fit it into a single day trip alongside the in-town sights makes the schedule too tight — we'd save it for a separate trip.

faq.q: Can you do Suphan Buri as a day trip from Bangkok?
faq.a: Easily. It's about 100 km — a 1.5- to 2-hour drive. If you leave Bangkok before 8 am and head back before 5 pm, you'll have a full day in town without needing to stay overnight.

faq.q: What is there to see in central Suphan Buri?
faq.a: The main sights are Wat Pa Lelai Worawihan, Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat, the Banharn–Jaemsai Tower, and Dragon Descendants Park. These all sit close together, no more than 15–20 minutes apart by car. Sam Chuk Market is just outside town, about 20–25 km away.

faq.q: Can I visit Suphan Buri without my own car?
faq.a: Yes — there are minivans and coaches from Mo Chit 2 and the new Southern terminal, with fares around 100–180 THB. But the in-town sights are spread out, so without a car you'll need motorbike taxis or to hire a ride between stops. Driving yourself is far more convenient for a day trip.

faq.q: What food should I try in Suphan Buri?
faq.a: Boat noodles are the province's signature dish, at around 15–25 THB a bowl. At Sam Chuk Market you'll find old-school shops like Jek Ao wonton noodles and Rang Sriroj, plus Mae Kim Liang sponge cake, which is a popular souvenir.

faq.q: How much should I budget for a Suphan Buri day trip?
faq.a: If you drive yourself, your main costs are fuel and tolls. Entry to each sight runs around 30 THB per person, plus food and souvenirs. All up it comes to a few hundred baht per person — an easy trip to keep on budget.
